info.bio: Kendrick Lamar Duckworth (17 Junio, 1987), es un rapero y cantautor americano nacido en Compton, California perteneciente a la firma Aftermath Entertainment. Consiguió llamar la atención después del lanzamiento en 2010 de su mixtape Overly Dedicated. En 2011, su album Section.80, lanzado exclusivamente a través de iTunes, se clasificó al instante como uno de los top lanzamientos digitales del año. Lamar ha acumulado un gran número de seguidores en internet y actualmente es miembro del grupo de Hip Hop Black Hippy

scenes.name: Grammys, Óscars, Hall of Fame y el Pulitzer
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Los grandes premios rechazaron o reconocieron tarde al hip hop. En los Grammy de 1984, la noche de Thriller, Herbie Hancock tocó «Rockit» con Grand Mixer D.ST en los platos: para Paradise Gray, la primera vez que se vio en la tele. En 1989 se creó el Grammy al mejor rap pero se entregó fuera de la retransmisión: Def Jam y Rush encabezaron el boicot y DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince no fueron a recoger el premio por «Parents Just Don’t Understand»; Kool Moe Dee sí fue, harto de que nadie hablara de estrategia («¿no decíamos que nos importaba un carajo el Grammy?»). En 1990 Young MC lo ganó en directo a «Fight the Power» y Flavor Flav le asaltó el escenario. Eminem fue el primer rapero en ganar un Óscar con «Lose Yourself» (2003, con Luis Resto), y Three 6 Mafia el segundo; Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five entraron los primeros en el Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (2007). En 2014 Macklemore se disculpó con Kendrick Lamar por ganarle; en 2018 DAMN. de Lamar, criado en Top Dawg por Punch, ganó el Pulitzer, algo que Nation of Millions habría merecido treinta años antes.

podcast.title: Comparison to Bob Dylan and Leonard Cohen
podcast.body: The lyrical depth and personal nature of Kendrick Lamar's work in *To Pimp a Butterfly* are compared to the early careers of Bob Dylan and Leonard Cohen. A New Musical Express writer suggested that if Bob Dylan were young and black today, he would be writing Kendrick Lamar's lyrics, noting similarities in how Dylan described his childhood, heartbreaking facts, and sad characters from his neighborhood. Kendrick Lamar is seen as reinventing this kind of profound, direct storytelling within black and hip hop culture. "posiblemente si Bob Dylan fue ese joven y fue ese negro hoy, estaría haciendo las letras que hay enriquezabar porque salvando las distancias no recuerdo un poco esa fase pues de Bob Dylan o incluso de Leonardo Coyne."

podcast.title: Early Artistic Development and Discovery
podcast.body: Kendrick Lamar began rapping at 16 years old, quickly demonstrating a mature style influenced by the old school, particularly West Coast sounds, NAS, Eminem, and Tupac. His early work showcased a highly technical mastery of poetry and a humble, direct style, contrasting with the gangsta rap he drew inspiration from. Before turning 18, he was discovered by Snoop Dogg and Dr. Dre, who are described as the "King Midas of modern rap," leading to collaborations with major artists like Snoop Dogg, Reysa, Asad Rocky, and Tutchains while still underage. "un joven de 16 años que empieza ya muy joven a rapear y que ya desde muy joven destaca muchísimo."

podcast.title: Elaborate Collaborative Process for *To Pimp a Butterfly*
podcast.body: For his album *To Pimp a Butterfly*, Kendrick Lamar dedicated two years to traveling globally, seeking out specific individuals needed for his complex musical vision. He didn't compose or create everything himself but acted as a "master of ceremonies," guiding a diverse array of artists, including lyricists, trumpeters, and guitarists, with his central idea. These collaborators contributed significantly to the album's immense creativity, making it a collective work under Kendrick Lamar's principal concept rather than solely his own. "Kendrick Lamar lo curioso es que no lo compone o no lo hace todo él, sino que actúa casi como un maestro de ceremonias."

podcast.title: Lyrical Depth and Social Commentary
podcast.body: Kendrick Lamar's lyrics, which were already notable in his youth for being influenced by West Coast and classic gangsta rap without being unrealistic or solely focused on violence, reached a new level in *To Pimp a Butterfly*. The album's lyrics are described as current, committed, and deeply political, addressing specific racial killings in the United States with names, surnames, and locations, and discussing the new crack epidemic. He also critically examines societal reactions and self-critique. "Las letras son actuales, son comprometidas, son políticas."

podcast.title: Personal and Self-Critical Lyrical Style
podcast.body: The lyrical approach in *To Pimp a Butterfly* is extraordinarily personal, akin to reading an artist's private diary. Kendrick Lamar delves into his own thoughts and feelings, including self-criticism, and discusses personal traumas from his American suburban upbringing that persist despite his success. His willingness to make such personal details public is highlighted as a rare and impactful characteristic, drawing comparisons to artists like Bob Dylan and Leonard Cohen. "él se critica enormemente a sí mismo reflexione enormemente sobre sí mismo."

podcast.title: Prince's Unfulfilled Collaboration on *To Pimp a Butterfly*

He later expressed regret over not being able to contribute to the album when he met Kendrick Lamar, indicating the widespread recognition of the project's significance. "el caso de Prince que Iba trabaja en Tutpim a Butterfly, pero al final pues por problemas de tiempo y de agendas no pudo."

xref.title: Career as Music Video Director
xref.body: Director X is recognized as one of the biggest music video directors globally, credited with creating "game-changing videos" for numerous renowned artists. He has been active in the industry for over 20 years, maintaining relevance since the late 1990s. His production company, Fella, achieved a breakthrough with the "Popstar" music video.
